Neoconservatism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Kristol and Kagan: A Neo-Reaganite Foreign Policy (1996)
quoteSource.citation: William Kristol and Robert Kagan, “Toward a Neo-Reaganite Foreign Policy,” Foreign Affairs 75(4), July/August 1996, pp. 18–32; especially “Benevolent Hegemony” and “Three Imperatives.” Carnegie reprint. Scope: this 1996 foreign-policy program, not every historical strand of neoconservatism.
quoteSource.note: Sourced editorial summary; not a quotation.

Neoliberalism.name: Neoliberalism
Neoliberalism.quote: Milton Friedman’s 1962 liberalism centers private property, competitive markets and limits on government power. Government still enforces market rules, addresses some market failures and supports low incomes through a negative income tax—cash payments below an income threshold. Unlike a strictly minimal state, this program allows a public income floor. It does not prescribe one foreign policy.
Neoliberalism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Friedman: Capitalism and Freedom (1962)
quoteSource.citation: Milton Friedman, Capitalism and Freedom (1962), Ch. II, pp. 34–36, and Ch. XII, pp. 190–195. The income floor depends on the tax-funded amount adopted. Scope: Friedman’s 1962 program; “neoliberalism” has contested broader uses. See Kevin Vallier, “Neoliberalism,” Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, introduction and §6.
quoteSource.note: Sourced editorial summary; not a quotation.

Neolibertarianism.name: Neolibertarianism
Neolibertarianism.quote: I am a hard-line interventionist to prevent massive democide and ensure American national security.
Neolibertarianism.author: R. J. Rummel
Neolibertarianism.description: This result uses R. J. Rummel’s 2005 position: qualified domestic libertarianism combined with military intervention abroad to oppose mass killing and promote democracy. Its distinguishing commitment is interventionist foreign policy; supporting private military firms alone does not establish this position.

quoteSource.label: Libertarianism Is Out — Neolibertarian Is In (2005)
quoteSource.citation: R. J. Rummel, first published March 31, 2005; reposted December 15, 2008, opening paragraphs. Quote is a contiguous excerpt from the second paragraph.
quoteSource.note: Excerpt; original wording retained.

Neosocialism.name: Neosocialism
Neosocialism.author: Adrien Marquet, SFIO congress (1933)
Neosocialism.description: This result represents French neo-socialism around the 1933 split from the SFIO. It sought a planned mixed economy and an alliance of workers and middle classes within a national framework. Unlike Park’s developmentalism, it presented planning as an intermediate step toward socialism. Its early parliamentary politics should not be confused with Déat’s later Nazi collaboration.

quoteSource.label: Neo-socialism: the 1933 watchwords
quoteSource.citation: Mathieu Hikaru Desan, Order, Authority, Nation (Cambridge University Press, 2026), Introduction, discussion of Marquet at the July 1933 SFIO congress; cites Parti Socialiste SFIO (1933), pp. 305–317, and Montagnon et al., Néo-socialisme ? (1933).
quoteSource.note: English rendering of “ordre, autorité, nation,” attributed through scholarship; the original congress transcript has not been independently checked.

Niekischism.name: Niekischism
Niekischism.quote: We are not communists, but for the sake of the nation we are capable of communism.
Niekischism.author: Ernst Niekisch

quoteSource.label: Quoted in DIE ZEIT (1974)
quoteSource.note: Translated from German for this site.
quoteSource.citation: Wolfgang Venohr, “Testament eines Patrioten,” DIE ZEIT, June 14, 1974, page 2. Retrospective quotation attributed to Ernst Niekisch; the original speech date is not specified.

Nilssonianism.name: Nilssonianism
Nilssonianism.quote: Every man should, as far as possible, be his own Jarl.
Nilssonianism.author: Jonas Nilsson

Noocracy.name: Noocracy
Noocracy.quote: If you do not take an interest in the affairs of your government, then you are doomed to live under the rule of fools.
Noocracy.author: Plato

Objectivism.name: Objectivism
Objectivism.quote: The pursuit of his own rational self-interest and of his own happiness is the highest moral purpose of his life.
Objectivism.author: Ayn Rand
Objectivism.description: Ayn Rand’s philosophy joins objective reality, reason and rational self-interest to laissez-faire capitalism and a government confined to protecting individual rights. It is more specific than minarchism: agreement about a minimal state alone does not imply agreement with Rand’s philosophical and ethical foundations.

quoteSource.label: Introducing Objectivism (1962)
quoteSource.citation: Ayn Rand, “Introducing Objectivism”, Los Angeles Times, June 17, 1962; Ayn Rand Institute transcription, numbered propositions 1–4 and following political paragraphs. Quote: proposition 3.

Ordoliberalism.name: Ordoliberalism
Ordoliberalism.quote: The processes peculiar to economic life in a free society make evident the fundamental superiority of the spontaneous order over the commanded order.
Ordoliberalism.author: Wilhelm Röpke

Orthodox Marxism.name: Orthodox Marxism
Orthodox Marxism.quote: As things stand today capitalist civilization cannot continue; we must either move forward into socialism or fall back into barbarism.
Orthodox Marxism.author: Karl Kautsky
Orthodox Marxism.description: Karl Kautsky’s Marxism before the First World War combined socialist theory with an independent mass workers’ party and trade-union struggle. The working class would win political power and establish social ownership. State ownership alone was not socialism: the capitalist character of the state had to change.

quoteSource.label: The Class Struggle (1892)
quoteSource.citation: Karl Kautsky, The Class Struggle (Erfurt Program), Chapter IV, §6, “The Structure of the Future State.” English translation by William E. Bohn, Charles H. Kerr & Company, 1910. Description: Chapter IV, §5, and Chapter V, §§9–12. Scope: Kautsky’s Marxism before the First World War, not every current called orthodox Marxism.

Orthodox Trotskyism.name: Orthodox Trotskyism
Orthodox Trotskyism.quote: The dictatorship of the proletariat which has risen to power as the leader of the democratic revolution is inevitably and, very quickly confronted with tasks, the fulfillment of which is bound up with deep inroads into the rights of bourgeois property. The democratic revolution grows over directly into the socialist revolution and thereby becomes a permanent revolution.
Orthodox Trotskyism.author: Lev Davidovich Bronstein

Owenism.name: Owenism
Owenism.quote: Union and cooperation in war obviously increase the power of the individual a thousand fold. Is there the shadow of a reason why they should not produce equal effects in peace?
Owenism.author: Robert Owen

Paleoconservatism.name: Paleoconservatism
Paleoconservatism.quote: A government's denial to its citizens of their right to limit citizenship on any grounds they see fit indicates not a democratic but an imperial order.
Paleoconservatism.author: Paul Edward Gottfried

Paleolibertarianism.name: Paleolibertarianism
Paleolibertarianism.quote: Natural authority arises from voluntary social structures; unnatural authority is imposed by the State.
Paleolibertarianism.author: Llewellyn H. Rockwell Jr.
Paleolibertarianism.description: This result covers Rockwell’s 1990 programme: free markets, private property and opposition to welfare and military intervention, joined to an explicitly traditionalist cultural strategy. Family, church and community authority should sustain liberty. His distinction between social authority and state coercion matters: cultural traditionalism does not itself authorize government enforcement.

quoteSource.label: The Case for Paleo-Libertarianism (1990)
quoteSource.citation: Llewellyn H. Rockwell Jr., Liberty 3(3), January 1990, pp. 34–38; principles I–X, p. 35; “Authority vs Coercion”, p. 36. Quote: p. 36.

Participism.name: Participism
Participism.quote: There is nothing truthful, wise, humane, or strategic about confusing hostility to injustice and oppression, which is leftist, with hostility to science and rationality, which is nonsense.
Participism.author: Michael Albert

Paternalistic conservatism.name: Paternalistic conservatism
Paternalistic conservatism.quote: The greatest good you can do for another is not just to share your riches but to reveal to him his own.
Paternalistic conservatism.author: Benjamin Disraeli

Patronalism.name: Patronalism
Patronalism.quote: It's better to be hanged for loyalty than rewarded for betrayal.
Patronalism.author: Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin

Personal autocracy.name: Personal autocracy
Personal autocracy.quote: If you must break the law, do it to seize power. In all other cases, observe it.
Personal autocracy.author: Gaius Julius Caesar

Platformism.name: Platformism
Platformism.quote: There is no such thing as harmless power.
Platformism.author: Nestor Ivanovych Makhno

Platonic timocracy.name: Platonic timocracy
Platonic timocracy.quote: Now put your shields before your hearts, and fight with hearts more proof than shields.
Platonic timocracy.author: Coriolanus

Political Futurism.name: Political Futurism
Political Futurism.quote: We intend to free this nation from its fetid cancer of professors, archaeologists, tour guides, and antiquarians.
Political Futurism.author: Emilio Angelo Carlo Marinetti

Posadism.name: Posadism
Posadism.quote: Atomic war is inevitable. It will destroy half of humanity. It is going to destroy immense human riches. Atomic war is going to provoke a true inferno on Earth. But it will not impede communism.
Posadism.author: Homero Rómulo Cristalli Frasnelli

Post-Autonomism.name: Post-Autonomism
Post-Autonomism.quote: The multitude is not a unity but a plurality of singularities acting in common.
Post-Autonomism.author: Antonio Negri

Post-Civilization.name: Post-Civilization
Post-Civilization.quote: We’re not primitivists: primitivists reject technology. We reject the inappropriate use of technology.
Post-Civilization.author: Strangers in a Tangled Wilderness

Progressive liberalism.name: Progressive liberalism
Progressive liberalism.quote: Democracy has to be born anew every generation, and education is its midwife.
Progressive liberalism.author: John Dewey

Proudhonian Mutualism.name: Proudhonian Mutualism
Proudhonian Mutualism.quote: As man seeks justice in equality, so society seeks order in anarchy.
Proudhonian Mutualism.author: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
Proudhonian Mutualism.description: This result covers Proudhon’s 1851 programme: reciprocal credit at cost, exchange between producers and workers’ associations where production requires collective labour. Small producers can remain independent. Unlike Tucker, he treats worker ownership and self-government in large industry as necessary.

quoteSource.label: What Is Property? (1840), chapter V
quoteSource.note: Benjamin R. Tucker translation. Programme: General Idea of the Revolution (1851), studies V–VII.
quoteSource.citation: P.-J. Proudhon, What Is Property? (1840), first memoir, chapter V, part II, paragraph beginning “And just as the right of force”; Benjamin R. Tucker translation, 1890 Humboldt edition as identified by this transcription. The quotation predates the scoped 1851 programme.

Reactionary Esotericism.name: Reactionary Esotericism
Reactionary Esotericism.quote: No idea is as absurd as the idea of progress.
Reactionary Esotericism.author: Julius Evola
Reactionary Esotericism.description: An esoteric traditionalist rejection of modern egalitarian society. This result emphasizes preserving spiritual independence and an inner hierarchy rather than immediately rebuilding political authority.

quoteSource.label: Revolt Against the Modern World
quoteSource.citation: Julius Evola, Revolt Against the Modern World, publisher’s excerpt.

Reactionaryism.name: Reactionaryism
Reactionaryism.quote: The people count for nothing in revolutions, or at most count only as a passive instrument.
Reactionaryism.author: Joseph Marie de Maistre
Reactionaryism.description: A politics of restoring the inherited monarchical, religious and hierarchical order displaced by modern revolution, rather than conserving the institutions of the present.

Religious Corporatism.name: Religious Corporatism
Religious Corporatism.quote: The social policy of the State, therefore, must devote itself to the re-establishment of the Industries and Professions.
Religious Corporatism.author: Pope Pius XI
Religious Corporatism.description: A religiously grounded social order organized through occupational bodies that coordinate employers and workers, mediate social interests and serve a common moral purpose.

quoteSource.label: Quadragesimo anno, §82
quoteSource.citation: Pius XI, Quadragesimo anno (1931), paragraph 82.

Right-libertarianism.name: Right-libertarianism
Right-libertarianism.quote: Consenting adults should be free to choose their own sexual practices and personal relationships.
Right-libertarianism.author: Libertarian Party (2016 platform)
Right-libertarianism.description: The 2016 U.S. Libertarian Party platform illustrates this broad result: private property, voluntary exchange, civil liberties and nonintervention abroad. It leaves personal choices to individuals without making approval of those choices a condition of liberty. This broad tradition overlaps minarchism and other libertarian results; it is not defined by rejecting them.

quoteSource.label: Libertarian Party platform (2016)
quoteSource.citation: Libertarian Party, platform adopted May 2016, preamble and §§1.4, 1.6, 2.0, 2.7, 2.11, 3.0–3.3; historical transcription in the party’s LPedia archive. Quote: §1.4.

Saint-Simonianism.name: Saint-Simonianism
Saint-Simonianism.quote: Today, for the first time since the existence of societies, it is a matter of organizing a totally new system, of replacing the celestial with the terrestrial, the vague by the positive, and the poetic by the real.
Saint-Simonianism.author: Claude Henri de Rouvroy

Schmittianism.name: Schmittianism
Schmittianism.quote: Sovereign is he who decides on the exception.
Schmittianism.author: Carl Schmitt
Schmittianism.description: A conception of political sovereignty centered on the authority to decide when normal law must be suspended, placing the decisive political act behind constitutional rules.

Scholar-bureaucracy.name: Scholar-bureaucracy
Scholar-bureaucracy.quote: To govern is to correct. If you set an example by being correct, who would dare to remain incorrect?
Scholar-bureaucracy.author: Confucius

Shachtmanism.name: Shachtmanism
Shachtmanism.quote: In the Soviet Union, control of the state, sole owner of social property, makes the bureaucracy the most powerful economic class.
Shachtmanism.author: Max Shachtman
Shachtmanism.description: The revolutionary Third Camp current that interpreted the Soviet bureaucracy as a new exploiting ruling class in a collectivized society, rejecting both capitalism and Stalinism.

quoteSource.label: Is Russia a Workers’ State? (1940)
quoteSource.citation: Max Shachtman, “Is Russia a Workers’ State?”, New International, December 1940.

Siegism.name: Siegism
Siegism.quote: Siegism is a neo-Nazi accelerationist tendency inspired by James Mason’s Siege editorials from the 1980s and their later circulation. It rejects conventional party politics and promotes self-directed terrorist violence to destabilize the existing political order and hasten its collapse. What distinguishes this current is decentralized accelerationist violence, not simply militancy or an association with guerrilla warfare.
Siegism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Johnson and Feldman (2023); ICCT (2021)
quoteSource.citation: Bethan Johnson and Matthew Feldman, “Siege: ‘Sheer Political Terror’,” Studies in Conflict & Terrorism, published online 2023, print 49, no. 1 (2026): 4–24, DOI 10.1080/1057610X.2023.2195061; Bethan Johnson, “Siege Culture After Siege: Anatomy of a Neo-Nazi Terrorist Doctrine,” International Centre for Counter-Terrorism, July 21, 2021.
quoteSource.note: Scholarly description of violent extremist doctrine, not an endorsement. The previous quote attributed to James Mason had no precise publication location and did not explain the result or separate it from its neighbors.

Social Autocracy / Social Authoritariani.name: Social Autocracy / Social Authoritarianism
Social Autocracy / Social Authoritariani.quote: For our friends, everything. For our enemies, not even justice.
Social Autocracy / Social Authoritariani.author: Juan Domingo Perón

Social corporatism.name: Social corporatism
Social corporatism.quote: We do not regard democratic society as the enemy of the individual, but as an instrument for the cooperation of individuals to protect their security and to support their personal development.
Social corporatism.author: Tage Fritjof Erlander

Social Credit.name: Social Credit
Social Credit.quote: Systems were made for men, and not men for systems.
Social Credit.author: Clifford Hugh Douglas
Social Credit.description: C. H. Douglas’s monetary reform program, using publicly created credit and a universal dividend to bring consumer purchasing power into line with productive capacity.

quoteSource.label: Economic Democracy, chapter 1
quoteSource.citation: C. H. Douglas, Economic Democracy (1920), chapter 1.

Social democracy.name: Social democracy
Social democracy.quote: The increase of social wealth is not accompanied by a diminishing number of capitalist magnates, but by an increasing number of capitalists of all degrees.
Social democracy.author: Eduard Bernstein

Social distributism.name: Social distributism
Social distributism.quote: To be clever enough to get all that money, one must be stupid enough to want it.
Social distributism.author: Gilbert Keith Chesterton

Social georgism.name: Social georgism
Social georgism.quote: Man is the only animal whose desires increase as they are fed, the only animal that is never satisfied.
Social georgism.author: Henry George

Social liberalism.name: Social liberalism
Social liberalism.quote: True individual freedom cannot exist without economic security and independence. People who are hungry and out of a job are the stuff of which dictatorships are made.
Social liberalism.author: Franklin Delano Roosevelt

Social libertarianism.name: Social libertarianism
Social libertarianism.quote: the best libertarian defense of property rights actually supports a welfare state -- in particular, a universal basic income.
Social libertarianism.author: Matt Zwolinski
Social libertarianism.description: This result covers the basic-income strand of libertarianism, illustrated by Matt Zwolinski’s 2015 argument. It defends a universal income floor on libertarian grounds rather than treating all state-funded welfare as a violation of property rights. This is one strand of the broader label, not a classification of every basic-income supporter.

quoteSource.label: The Libertarian Case for a Basic Income for All (2015)
quoteSource.citation: Matt Zwolinski, “Property Rights, Coercion, and the Welfare State: The Libertarian Case for a Basic Income for All” (2015), author’s abstract in University of San Diego repository. Full paper unavailable in this retrieval.
quoteSource.note: Excerpt; original wording retained.

Socialism of the 21st Century.name: Socialism of the 21st Century
Socialism of the 21st Century.quote: Capitalism is the road to hell, to the destruction of the world.
Socialism of the 21st Century.author: Hugo Chávez

Sorelianism.name: Sorelianism
Sorelianism.quote: By accepting the idea of the general strike, although we know that it is a myth, we are proceeding exactly as a modern physicist does who has complete confidence in his science.
Sorelianism.author: Georges Eugène Sorel

Spartacism (Luxemburgism).name: Spartacism (Luxemburgism)
Spartacism (Luxemburgism).quote: Freedom is always and exclusively freedom for the one who thinks differently.
Spartacism (Luxemburgism).author: Rosa Luxemburg

Stakeholder capitalism.name: Stakeholder capitalism
Stakeholder capitalism.quote: In the Davos Manifesto 2020, companies serve employees, customers, suppliers, communities and shareholders. Their performance includes social and environmental responsibilities as well as financial returns. This concerns corporate purpose, not whether the state or private investors own a company; it can coexist with state capitalism.
Stakeholder capitalism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Davos Manifesto 2020
quoteSource.citation: Klaus Schwab, Davos Manifesto 2020, 2 December 2019, sections A–C. This card scopes the WEF formulation; it does not represent every stakeholder theory.

State capitalism.name: State capitalism
State capitalism.quote: State capitalism combines state ownership of capital with commercial enterprise. In Singapore’s Temasek model, described in 2013, the government owns the investment company but does not direct its individual investment decisions. This concerns ownership and investment governance, not a rejection of responsibilities to workers, communities or other stakeholders.
State capitalism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Temasek: ownership and governance (2013)
quoteSource.citation: Lim Boon Heng, 4th Annual Sovereign Wealth Fund Conference, 5 December 2013: opening description; Government as a shareholder; social responsibility. Singapore is one model, not a definition of all state capitalism.

State corporatism.name: State corporatism
State corporatism.quote: This result uses Portugal’s 1933 constitutional programme as a representative case. The state coordinates economic life through recognized occupational bodies, subordinating their interests to national policy while protecting private property. Its distinguishing institution is state-directed representation of organized economic interests, rather than workers’ acquisition of property or an industrial investment plan alone.
State corporatism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Portuguese Constitution (1933)
quoteSource.citation: Constitution of 11 April 1933, original text, arts. 8(15), 31–34; Portuguese Assembly of the Republic facsimile. Editorial summary, not a quotation by Salazar.
quoteSource.note: A constitutional programme, not a claim that every promise was implemented.

State socialism.name: State socialism
State socialism.quote: If you own the things men must have, you own the men who must have them.
State socialism.author: Edward Bellamy

Strasserism.name: Strasserism
Strasserism.quote: We must take from the right nationalism without capitalism and from the left socialism without internationalism.
Strasserism.author: Gregor Strasser

Stratocracy.name: Stratocracy
Stratocracy.quote: I have not the particular shining bauble or feather in my cap for crowds to gaze at or kneel to, but I have power and resolution for foes to tremble at.
Stratocracy.author: Oliver Cromwell

Superfascism.name: Superfascism
Superfascism.quote: The legionary spirit is that fire of one who will choose the hardest road, who will fight to the death even when all is already lost.
Superfascism.author: Giulio Cesare Andrea Evola

Surrealism.name: Surrealism
Surrealism.quote: Beauty will be convulsive or it will not be at all.
Surrealism.author: André Breton

Syndicalism.name: Syndicalism
Syndicalism.quote: The proletariat alone embodies the creative forces of society. The bourgeoisie represents only the forces of decay.
Syndicalism.author: Édouard Berth

Synthesis Anarchism.name: Synthesis Anarchism
Synthesis Anarchism.quote: I think the question is not about communists and individualists, but rather about anarchists and non-anarchists.
Synthesis Anarchism.author: Errico Malatesta

Technocracy.name: Technocracy
Technocracy.quote: We owe nothing in our origins to any political philosophers. We do owe a debt to a thousand American chemists, engineers, scientists, and technologists.
Technocracy.author: Howard Scott

Theocracy.name: Theocracy
Theocracy.quote: He who doesn't pray to the Lord prays to the devil.
Theocracy.author: Jorge Mario Bergoglio

Third international theory.name: Third international theory
Third international theory.quote: For 40 years, I have not been the ruler. The authority has been with the people. They take nothing from me or add anything to me.
Third international theory.author: Muammar Muhammad Abu Minyar al-Gaddafi

Third way.name: Third way
Third way.quote: Tony Blair and Gerhard Schröder’s 1999 Third Way combines competitive markets with an active welfare state. It emphasizes education, training, employment and support for enterprise, while linking help for people able to work to responsibilities to take up work or training. Its approach to poverty centers on employment and public services as well as cash support.
Third way.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Blair and Schröder: The Third Way (1999)
quoteSource.citation: Tony Blair and Gerhard Schröder, Europe: The Third Way / Die Neue Mitte, 8 June 1999, §§III–IV. This description covers their joint program, including active government, flexible markets, lifelong learning and rights and responsibilities in labour-market policy.
quoteSource.note: Sourced editorial summary; not a quotation.

Titoism.name: Titoism
Titoism.quote: State ownership is the lowest form of social ownership, and not the highest as the leaders of the USSR consider it to be.
Titoism.author: Josip Broz Tito
Titoism.description: This result covers Yugoslavia’s 1965 market-reform programme: social ownership, workers’ councils and enterprise markets under the League of Communists. It decentralizes economic decisions while retaining public planning and excluding rival parties from government. This specific reform programme does not represent every phase of Yugoslav socialism.

quoteSource.label: Workers Manage Factories in Yugoslavia (1950)
quoteSource.note: Speech of 26 June 1950; an earlier statement on workers’ management.
quoteSource.citation: Josip Broz Tito, Workers Manage Factories in Yugoslavia, 26 June 1950, “Role of the Trade Unions”; MIA transcription of the Belgrade 1950 pamphlet, pp. 4–43. Translator not identified. The quotation precedes the period classified by this result.

Tridemism.name: Tridemism
Tridemism.quote: For forty years, I have devoted myself to the cause of the people's revolution with but one aim in view - the elevation of China to a position of freedom and equality among the nations.
Tridemism.author: Sun Yat-sen

Tripartite corporatism.name: Tripartite corporatism
Tripartite corporatism.quote: Labor is not fighting for a larger slice of the national pie. Labor is fighting for a larger pie.
Tripartite corporatism.author: Walter Philip Reuther

Tuckerite Mutualism.name: Tuckerite Mutualism
Tuckerite Mutualism.quote: A just distribution of the products of labor is to be obtained by destroying all sources of income except labor.
Tuckerite Mutualism.author: Benjamin Tucker

quoteSource.label: Solutions of the Labor Problem (1891)
quoteSource.citation: Benjamin Tucker, “Solutions of the Labor Problem,” Liberty, September 12, 1891; reprinted in Instead of a Book (1893/1897), paragraph 20.

Tuckerite Mutualism.description: This result covers Tucker’s 1888–91 programme: free banking, occupancy-based land tenure and free exchange should end monopoly income. He expects interest beyond lending costs to disappear. Unlike Proudhon, he allows freely chosen wage employment as well as workers’ associations.

Voluntaryism.name: Voluntaryism
Voluntaryism.quote: Voluntaryists are advocates of non-political, non-violent strategies to achieve a free society.
Voluntaryism.author: Carl Watner
Voluntaryism.description: A private-property anarchist approach that seeks a society of voluntary relations through education, nonviolent resistance and withdrawal of cooperation from the state.

quoteSource.label: Introduction to the Non-Voting Series
quoteSource.citation: Carl Watner, “Introduction to the Non-Voting Series” (November 2015).

Vperedism.name: Vperedism
Vperedism.quote: The revolution is not merely an economic or political event; it is also a cultural and moral one.
Vperedism.author: Alexander Vasilyevich Bogdanov

Workers’ Oppositionism.name: Workers’ Oppositionism
Workers’ Oppositionism.quote: The Workers’ Opposition relies on the creative powers of its own class: the workers.
Workers’ Oppositionism.author: Alexandra Kollontai
Workers’ Oppositionism.description: The Bolshevik opposition current calling for industrial unions and workers’ elected bodies to direct the economy, resisting bureaucratic administration while retaining communist political leadership.

quoteSource.label: The Workers’ Opposition, chapter 2
quoteSource.citation: Alexandra Kollontai, The Workers’ Opposition (1921), “The Trade Unions: Their Role and Problems.”

World State (Brave New World).name: World State (Brave New World)
World State (Brave New World).quote: In Aldous Huxley’s Brave New World (1932), the World State engineers a caste hierarchy and conditions people to accept their assigned lives. Consumer pleasures, sleep-teaching, and the drug soma help suppress discontent. Unlike Ingsoc, it relies chiefly on managed contentment, though it also uses coercion and exile.
World State (Brave New World).author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Huxley: Brave New World (1932), chapters I–II and XVI
quoteSource.citation: Aldous Huxley, Brave New World (1932), chapters I–II (caste production and conditioning), XVI (Mustapha Mond on stability, soma and exile); Brave New World Revisited (1958), chapter I, opening comparison with Nineteen Eighty-Four.
quoteSource.note: Sourced description of a fictional regime, not Huxley’s political program. The alias refers to the novel’s Ford cult, not the historical Fordist system of mass production and consumption (Bob Jessop, “Fordism and Post-Fordism: a Critical Reformulation,” 1992, section I).

Yellow socialism.name: Yellow socialism
Yellow socialism.quote: This result represents Pierre Biétry’s French Yellow movement around 1904–1906. It advocated cooperation between employers and workers, profit sharing and workers becoming co-owners through association contracts. Its 1904 appeal relied on members’ own associations rather than public authorities to carry out this programme. Its nationalism included antisemitism. Unlike state corporatism, its distinctive proposal centered on workers acquiring property, rather than subordinating occupational bodies to the state. The historical label does not imply support for socialist ownership.
Yellow socialism.author: Editorial description

quoteSource.label: Le socialisme et les Jaunes (1906)
quoteSource.citation: Pierre Biétry, Le socialisme et les Jaunes, 8th ed. (1906), dedication pp. v–vi, opening pp. 1–3, congress programme pp. 264–267, and “Appel aux Jaunes de France,” pp. 321–324. Historical interpretation: Georges Ubbiali, review of Christophe Maillard’s thesis, Dissidences (2011), discussion of 1901–1908.
quoteSource.note: Editorial summary of the movement, not a quotation by Biétry.
